Subject: Pilot Health — production pilot ask (isolation/compliance)

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to move forward with a limited production pilot but need the data plane to be isolated for compliance. Key asks below:

- Isolation: customer-dedicated tenancy or VPC-hosted private deployment; no multi-tenant mixing with other customers.
- Throughput: sustained 40–60 requests/sec during business hours (PST), expected peak 90 reqs/sec.
- Prompts: average input ~1,200 tokens; average generation ~400 tokens.
- Concurrency: up to ~120 concurrent users in peak windows.
- Latency target: 95th <= 400ms for short prompts (<512 tokens); for full loads we can tolerate up to 800ms.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 Type II required, audit logs retained 1 year, encryption at rest + KMS integration.
- Timeline: pilot kickoff target 8 weeks out; procurement window ~3–4 weeks.

I've attached a short spreadsheet with hourly traffic slices and sample prompts. Can you outline what a Private vs Dedicated (reserved) hosting slate would look like, with a recommended GPU mix for the pilot and high-level cost delta? Also include any operational caveats (onboarding time, SLA differences, rollback/fallback patterns).

Thanks,
Daniel

Team — forwarding Daniel's requirements. I sketched two candidate slates below (quick back-of-envelope). Marissa / Karthik, please sanity-check and augment with ops notes.

OPTION A — Private (VPC + customer-managed nodes / private control plane)
- Service: Private deployment in customer's VPC, private control plane; KMS/HSM integration for keys.
- GPU slate (pilot): 3 x H100-80GB (preferred) or 4 x A100-80GB equivalent.
- Rationale: single-tenant hardware reduces blast radius, easier for strict compliance and KMS isolation.
- Performance estimate: 40–60 req/s sustained with p95 latency targets < 500ms on average prompt sizes if model is quantized to int8 and we enable KV/prefix caching. Handles brief bursts to ~120 req/s with pre-warmed nodes.
- Ops: ~6–8 week lead time (provisioning + network config + KMS attestation + SOC2 evidence review).
- Cost: higher procurement/infra uplift (fixed infra + on-call ops). Estimated delta vs Dedicated: +25–40% on monthly runrate for pilot depending on H/W choice.

OPTION B — Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved pool with isolation at tenant boundary)
- Service: Dedicated reserved GPU pool (single-tenant logical isolation), Redwood-managed control plane with strong tenant isolation, KMS integration via VPC peering.
- GPU slate (pilot): 6 x A100-80GB reserved with autoscale burst to 10 GPUs for marketing spikes.
- Rationale: faster onboarding (no infra procurement) and simpler ongoing ops; cost-efficient if usage consistent.
- Performance estimate: Sustained 50–70 req/s with p95 < 400–600ms; can burst to meet 150 req/s events with brief latency degradation.
- Ops: ~3–4 week onboarding (account setup, network peering, SOC2 docs).
- Cost: lower monthly commitment compared to Private; but less absolute isolation — acceptable for many regulated customers with specific controls.

Trade-offs / notes:
- Model quantization and batching can materially reduce GPU count. If we can pre-quantize to int8 or 4-bit, the Dedicated slate could drop from 6->4 GPUs in practice. Karthik: is 4-bit production-ready for this model?
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for common prompts (e.g., intake forms) reduces per-token compute and significantly lowers p95 tail.
- Fallbacks: we should propose an explicit fallback path to a lighter quantized variant in case of capacity strain.
- SLA: Dedicated reserved pool carries standard Redwood SLOs; Private deployments will require bespoke SLA negotiation and longer lead times.

Next steps: Marissa, can you confirm commercial appetite for a +25–40% private uplift? Karthik, can you provide a tighter ops sizing and an optimization checklist we can attach to the proposal? I'll draft an external brief for Daniel and procure to show options + cost delta.

Thanks,
Vanessa

Quick ops sanity check — high level notes:
- Model: Llama-3-8B is friendly to 4-bit quant (grouped quant + per-channel scales). We can run a short eval that measures latency/quality degradation; expect token throughput to improve ~1.8–2x vs fp16 when tuned.
- GPU mix: H100 is ideal for latency but procurement lead time is longer; A100 is reliable and available in Dedicated pools. For Private we should size for H100 if customer requires lowest p95.
- Sizing math (conservative): average generation 400 tokens + 1,200 input => ~1,600 tokens per request. At target 60 req/s sustained => 96k tokens/s.
  - With optimized kernels and token-parallelism on A100: one A100-80GB can sustain ~20–25k tokens/s for this model family when quantized + batching.
  - So Dedicated: 4 x A100 (25k * 4 = 100k tokens/s) covers sustained; reserve 2 additional GPUs for burst handling (total 6 with autoscale to 10 for marketing spikes).
  - Private (H100): 3 x H100 could cover the baseline with better latency headroom.
- KV cache and prefix caching: strongly recommend enabling customer-side session hashing to keep hot contexts cached on inference nodes. This cuts compute by ~20–30% for repeat flows.
- Onboarding tasks: network peering, KMS key exchange, egress review, SOC2 evidence collection, DR test for failover. Ops ETA: Dedicated ~2–3 weeks if legal/compliance docs are ready; Private ~6–9 weeks including node provisioning.
- Risk: if the customer runs unbounded generation (long chain-of-thought prompts) our token assumptions break — request a max-generation cap per session during pilot.

I'll assemble a short optimization checklist and a small perf runbook (latency vs token-rate charts) to include in the proposal.

Karthik
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
